guard: The engine seam enforces the same laws the walker enforces inline: the member laws (L4014/L4018/L4020), freeze-on-share in both halves (L2031/L2032), the fuel budget and its macrotask yield (L4013 + the cut), the thenable gate the walker cannot survive, the calling-convention adapter that exists only on this side (and the invariant that it is invisible from inside the program), the host's run wiring (source-pinned hash, the resume refusals, the run-bound effect ceiling), the concurrency scopes over the SHARED machinery (the calling-convention adapter on the arms, the bag's key, the deferred body, and the branch digest the engine has no AST to compute), the cell read (get's third argument, hasOwn rather than truthiness) and the loud clause that a native ReferenceError is the ENGINE's fault, the node floor (refused at the run boundary, by major version), and the worker: lockdown once per thread, a Compartment with zero endowments, the shared stop flag as the only cancellation channel, and what does and does not cross the boundary. (FAIL-FAST suite: markers are upstream of the cells they guard.)
why: These cells are first-party rather than differential, because the walker cannot grade them: the
fuel unit changes in languageVersion 2, the thenable programs kill the walker's host process, and
the calling-convention adapter has no walker counterpart. A first-party cell with no mutant is a
cell nobody has shown can fail, so every law the seam claims to hold gets a mutation here.
ONE CELL HERE HAS NO MUTANT, ON PURPOSE. `the library calls exactly the argument positions the
seam adapts` is a drift alarm on library.ts, which the engine may not edit: it probes every name in
every table with a marker and compares the positions the library ACTUALLY calls to the ones the
seam adapts. It is declaration-independent by construction, so mutating the seam's list cannot red
it - the two mutants that grade that list are the ones on `adaptArgs` and on the read form. Its own
failure mode, finding nothing at all, is graded by the count cell beside it.
THE COLD-START CELL HAS NO MUTANT EITHER, and for the same kind of reason as the drift alarm above:
it REPORTS the number in its own name and bounds it only loosely, because a tight bound on a shared
machine is a flaky cell rather than a rule. What the worker must actually do is graded by the eleven
mutants below it, every one of which leaves a run that still answers.
THE TWO DIVERGENCE CELLS IN THE SCOPE SECTION HAVE NO MUTANT HERE, and the reason is worth writing
down rather than leaving as a gap. `an edit inside a LOSING arm diverges on resume` grades the
COMPARISON, which lives in perform.ts and belongs to the shared machinery's own ledger. What this
file owns is that the digest handed to it is the walker's, and any mutation of that is caught one
cell earlier, as a journal difference on the live run - which is why both digest mutants below
name the journal cell rather than the divergence cell they would also break.
THE CLOSURE-OBLIGATION SECTION HAS NO MUTANT OF ITS OWN, for the same reason as the drift
alarm above: what it holds is a property of library.ts, which the engine may not edit, and it probes
the WHOLE builtin table behaviourally rather than reading a declaration - so nothing in the seam can
be mutated to break it. Its own failure mode, probing nothing, is graded by the count in the first
cell's name. The two gates that actually keep the door shut, born() and set() refusing a callable
`then`, are mutated where they live, further up this file.

mutations.completionMarker: ok a function callee passes through as itself
mutations.cell: calling a record is L4011

mutations.name: a branch shares its parent's key namespace instead of opening its own
mutations.expectRed: a branch frame allocates the walker's own step keys
mutations.completionMarker: ok a constructor read as a VALUE is a function, not L2001
mutations.cell: a branch frame allocates the walker's own step keys
mutations.note: Two branches running the same named effect would race for one occurrence counter, so which arm finished first would decide which step key each got - the journal would record a different pair of keys on every run and no resume could find either. The cell compares against the oracle's own keys for the same program rather than asserting a spelling.

mutations.name: a branch shares its parent's clock
mutations.expectRed: and moves without moving the parent's
mutations.completionMarker: ok a branch inherits the clock at the fork
mutations.cell: and moves without moving the parent's
mutations.note: The recorded clocks are what decide a race: an arm advances its own past the frontier and proves it cannot win. On one shared clock a sibling's effect moves every arm, so the frontier is whatever landed last and the winner is whoever the host scheduled.

mutations.name: a branch shares its parent's cancellation signal
mutations.expectRed: cancelling a branch does not cancel the run it branched from
mutations.completionMarker: ok the join takes the branch's history
mutations.cell: cancelling a branch does not cancel the run it branched from
mutations.note: A scope cancels its LOSERS. On a shared signal the first loser cancels the run that is still waiting for the winner, so a race would end every program that used one.

mutations.name: a conclave body raises the depth like a racing branch
mutations.expectRed: and a conclave body does NOT, because it has no sibling to race
mutations.completionMarker: ok a concurrent branch raises the depth
mutations.cell: and a conclave body does NOT, because it has no sibling to race
mutations.note: A conclave opens a scope but not a race: one body, nothing running beside it, so a write from inside it is as ordered as a write anywhere else. Under the mutant L2032 refuses writes that the walker allows, and the refusal names a nondeterminism that cannot occur.

mutations.name: a child signal does not inherit a parent that is already cancelled
mutations.expectRed: a child made after the cut starts cancelled AND cut
mutations.completionMarker: ok a repeated cancellation is not a third event
mutations.cell: a child made after the cut starts cancelled AND cut
mutations.note: A nested branch launched after its parent was cut is a branch that cannot win either, and it would otherwise run - and perform - with no cancellation at all, because the parent's cancel already fired before it subscribed.

mutations.name: a child signal never subscribes to its parent
mutations.expectRed: a parent's cancellation reaches the child
mutations.completionMarker: ok a child of a live signal starts live
mutations.cell: a parent's cancellation reaches the child
mutations.note: Cancellation flows down or it does nothing: a scope cancels the arm, and the arm's own nested branches keep running and keep performing against the world.

mutations.name: a soft cancellation can never be escalated to the cut
mutations.expectRed: and the ESCALATION reaches an already-cancelled child
mutations.completionMarker: ok softly, when the parent cancelled softly
mutations.cell: and the ESCALATION reaches an already-cancelled child
mutations.note: The walker re-decides the cut when a cancelled arm's own clock lands past the frontier - measured there as an infinite pure tail burning the whole step budget and killing a run whose race had already settled ok, while a resume of the same journal returned the winner. Without the escalation the engine cannot re-decide it either. The mutant is conditioned on `first` on purpose: dropping the escalation outright also breaks the FIRST cut, so it reddened the yield-boundary cell four sections earlier and graded a rule it was not aimed at. Conditioned, it leaves a fresh cut working and removes only the escalation of a signal already cancelled softly.

mutations.name: a later cancellation overwrites the reason the branch was cancelled for
mutations.expectRed: the reason stays the FIRST one, because that is what cancelled the branch
mutations.completionMarker: ok and the ESCALATION reaches an already-cancelled child
mutations.cell: the reason stays the FIRST one, because that is what cancelled the branch
mutations.note: The reason is what the Cancelled error carries out of the branch and into the trace. An escalation is not a new reason for stopping - the branch stopped when it lost - so overwriting it makes every cut arm report the escalation instead of the loss.

mutations.find: const list = typeof args === "function" ? await args() : args;
mutations.replace: const list = typeof args === "function" ? args() : args;

mutations.completionMarker: ok the confinement probe ran

mutations.completionMarker: ok the confinement probe ran

mutations.name: a run with no value is put through the rule about values
mutations.find: if (result.value !== undefined) assertCrossable(result.value, "the value this run returned");
mutations.expectRed: a run completes in its own locked-down thread, spawned from the BUILT package
mutations.completionMarker: ok a continuation without the optional flag is refused, not silently run
mutations.cell: a run completes in its own locked-down thread, spawned from the BUILT package
mutations.note: A program whose last line is a statement ends with NO value, and the walker reports exactly that. `assertCrossable` refuses undefined by design - it is a rule about values crossing an effect boundary, and absence is not a value - so applying it here refuses the ordinary case. Measured before the guard existed: the first worker cell written refused its own fixture.

mutations.name: a value that cannot cross is left to the structured-clone algorithm
mutations.find: if (result.value !== undefined) assertCrossable(result.value, "the value this run returned");
mutations.expectRed: and the refusal names the language's rule, not a clone algorithm
mutations.completionMarker: ok and it carries the reason the host wrote into shared memory
mutations.cell: and the refusal names the language's rule, not a clone algorithm
mutations.note: Unrefused, a function reaches `postMessage` and the clone fails. The thread no longer DIES on that: since the rethrow landed it ANSWERS with the DataCloneError, so the outcome cell is satisfied either way (`ok === false` holds for an answered refusal as much as a refused value) and the kill moved one cell downstream, onto the one that refuses a host algorithm's name where the language has a word of its own. Measured on two arms rather than reasoned: with the rethrow the outcome cell prints ok and the naming cell fails with {"name":"DataCloneError"}; at the commit before it, the thread exits and the host rejects at worker.ts:177 with `worker exited with code 0 before the run answered`, which reds the outcome cell instead. The general rule this cost us: a rethrow that converts a death into an answer moves every mutant's kill in that file one cell downstream, so re-grade a file's WHOLE config when a commit touches it, not just the entries the commit adds.

mutations.note: The bytes are written first and the LENGTH is what publishes them, so a reader can never see a length promising bytes the writer has not finished writing. Drop the store and the reader's atomic load answers 0 forever: the reason is in memory the run will never look at.

mutations.name: the reason is cut by bytes again, through a character
mutations.find: const { written } = new TextEncoder().encodeInto(reason === "" ? NO_REASON : reason, room);

mutations.completionMarker: ok and a reason past the buffer is truncated, not dropped
mutations.cell: a reason cut by the buffer is cut BETWEEN characters, never through one
mutations.note: The spelling this replaced, restored exactly. A UTF-8 character is one to four bytes and a cut placed by byte count alone lands inside one: measured through the real thread, a three-byte character straddling the buffer's last byte reached the run as U+FFFD on the end of the operator's sentence. `encodeInto` fills the room with whole code points and reports what that took. The truncation cell above stays green under this mutant - it only asks that a long reason is cut at all - which is why the cut's PLACE needs a cell and a mutant of its own.

The older spelling floored the length at 1 instead, which DID stop the run - and delivered whatever byte happened to be in shared memory, measured as a NUL on the end of the operator's sentence.
